subject: gk
question: Which of the following ancient Indian sites is famous for its chaityas and viharas carved into rock?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajanta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ajanta Caves** are located in the **Aurangabad district** of **Maharashtra** and comprise about **30 rock-cut Buddhist monuments** excavated into a **basaltic horseshoe-shaped cliff**.
 
• These caves were developed in two phases, starting from the **2nd century BCE** (**Satavahana period**) and continuing to the **5th and 6th centuries CE** (**Vakataka period**).
 
• The site is categorized into two main types of structures: **Chaityas**, which served as **prayer halls** containing a stupa, and **Viharas**, which were **monastic residential quarters** for monks.
 
• The **Chaitya halls** (such as Caves 9, 10, 19, and 26) feature vaulted ceilings and polished stone, while the **Viharas** consist of central halls surrounded by sleeping cells.
 
• The caves are famous for their **mural paintings** and sculptures that depict scenes from the **Jataka tales** and the various lives of **Gautama Buddha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thanjavur**:

 
 
• Located in **Tamil Nadu**, it was the capital of the **Medieval Cholas** and is home to the **Brihadisvara Temple**, built by **Raja Raja Chola I**.
 
 
 
• **Mahabalipuram**:
 
 
• Situated in **Tamil Nadu**, it is known for **Pallava rock-cut architecture**, including the **Pancha Rathas** and the **Shore Temple**, but it is primarily a Hindu site.
 
 
 
• **Hampi**:
 
 
• Located in **Karnataka**, it served as the capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire** and features structural temples like the **Virupaksha Temple** and the **Stone Chariot** at **Vittala Temple**.
